design.name_ko: 미니 시소 (밸런스 핀 + 꼬리 강철 추, 백건만 보조 스프링)
design.architecture: A one-piece PETG key is a seesaw on a steel cross pin (dowel 3x10) at y140/z27. The pin rests in a cloth-lined open notch on a 2 mm printed fin of a balance rail (y135-145). The fin also guides the key sideways. A 9x32 SS400 flat bar stands on edge in the key tail (y146-206.5): 50 mm (113 g) in white keys, 37 mm (84 g) in black keys. Rest (up-stop) uses the v3 front hook and tab unchanged; the tail weight holds the key crossbar up against the hook felt. The first down-stop is the steel bar hitting a 3T felt under a 'tail stop bar'. That bar is bolted into a groove in the rear wall at z51.3-56.2, and the felt sits in front of the centre of percussion, so the impact pushes the pin into its notch. The v3 front felt is a second down-stop 0.5 mm later and takes the finger force. Black keys return by gravity only. White keys get 48 % of the balance torque from gravity and the rest from a d0.4/OD6/L50 compression spring in a well at the tail end, seated in the stop bar. If a spring breaks, the key still returns (DW 25.3 g, UW 18.9 g). Sensor bar, magnets, hooks, dovetails and frame depth 212 are unchanged from v3. The control board moves under the key front arms (y94-133, cut to 39x70).
design.summary_ko: 건반 한 개를 강철 핀 위에 얹은 시소로 만들고, 꼬리에 강철 막대(평철 9×32)를 넣어 무게로 돌아오게 했다. 시소 전체가 v3의 212 mm 프레임 안에 들어가고 센서·자석·훅은 v3 그대로 쓴다. 흑건은 무게추만으로 돌아오지만, 백건은 앞팔이 길어서 무게추가 복귀 힘의 48 %만 내고 나머지는 작은 금속 스프링이 낸다. 다운웨이트 50 g, 재타건 30 Hz(백)·20 Hz(흑), 정지 상태 플라스틱 응력 0.66 MPa로 목표를 맞췄다. 대신 짧은 시소의 약점이 숫자로 드러났다. 앞/뒤 힘 비가 2.60(v3 2.2)이고, 백건 관성이 19 g으로 가벼우며, 88건반에 강철이 9.0 kg 든다. 스프링 없이 무게추만 쓰려면 앞/뒤 비 3.55를 받아들이거나 깊이를 39 mm 이상 늘려야 한다.
design.how_it_works_ko: 건반 가운데보다 조금 뒤(y140)에 박은 지름 3 mm 강철 핀이 프레임의 얇은 날개 위 홈에 얹혀 있고, 건반은 이 핀을 축으로 시소처럼 움직인다. 손을 떼면 꼬리의 강철 막대가 무거워서 앞이 올라가고, 앞쪽 v3 훅의 펠트에 닿아 멈춘다. 누르면 꼬리가 올라가 강철 막대가 위쪽 펠트에 부딪히며 멈추고, 0.5 mm 뒤에 앞 펠트가 손가락 힘을 받는다. 무거운 추가 직접 펠트에 멈추기 때문에 핀이 홈에서 튀어 오르는 힘이 거의 생기지 않는다. 백건은 무게만으로는 조금 모자라서 꼬리 끝 우물에 든 작은 압축 스프링이 나머지를 민다. 플라스틱은 늘 거의 힘을 받지 않아서(최대 0.66 MPa) 휘거나 처질 일이 없다.

risks: Heavy: 9.00 kg of steel for 88 keys. An octave module weighs about 1.87 kg against 0.59 kg in v3, which works against R18 (carry in parts).

White keys have low inertia (m_eff 19.4 g) and black keys 42.7 g, so the two feel different. The option of 4 steel balls in the white key head raises white to 31.0 g, but the spring preload goes up to 0.76 N and the gravity share falls to 17 %.
Front/back force ratio is 2.60, worse than v3 (2.2) and a grand (~1.5). Pressing a white key at y90 needs 130 g.

On hard strikes the pin hops out of its notch: 0.10 mm (white) / 0.17 mm (black) at 1 m/s and 0.23 / 0.33 mm at 1.5 m/s. It can tick unless the notch is lined with cloth; a harder tail felt (E 2.5 MPa) cuts this to 0.028 mm.
The key bounces 0.82 mm (white) / 1.08 mm (black) off the hook felt on return and settles within +-0.2 mm after 52 / 85 ms. The firmware thresholds must ignore this.
The real stiffness of the stock spring is unknown (the calc assumes 40 active coils, k 0.036 N/mm). It must be measured, and preload set with a well spacer (+1.81 g DW per mm).
Tab bushing friction (2.98 g of the 3.79 g) is an assumed 0.05 N per side preload.
88 steel bars must be cut by hand (estimated 2-3 h), or outsourced at about 264,000 won.
Black keels sit at z9.01, only 4 mm above the floor. Cables or debris under the tails would jam keys.

White keys cannot return by gravity alone inside 212 mm with a playable ratio. Pure gravity needs pivot y122 (ratio 3.55, magnet travel 4.57 mm, control board space only 21 mm) or a frame 39-49 mm deeper with 7.8-9.6 kg of steel.
assembly_ko: 평철 9×32를 백건용 50 mm 52개, 흑건용 37 mm 36개로 자르고 모서리를 다듬는다(88회 절단).
건반을 윗면을 베드에 대고 뽑는다. v3 방식으로 자석을 붙이고, 평행핀 Ø3×10을 보스 구멍 Ø3.05에 CA로 붙이고, 강철 막대를 꼬리 주머니에 에폭시로 붙인다.
프레임에 v3 앞 펠트와 훅 펠트를 붙이고, 날개 홈 12곳에 천 0.5T를, 꼬리 스톱 바 아래에 펠트 3T 띠를 붙인다.
백건 꼬리 우물에 스프링을 넣는다(울림 방지로 그리스 한 방울).
건반을 제자리보다 3.5 mm 앞에 내려놓고 뒤로 민다. 핀이 날개 홈에 떨어지고 크로스바가 훅 밑으로 들어간다.
꼬리 스톱 바를 뒷벽 홈에 끼우고 스프링 윗끝을 포켓에 맞춘 뒤 손나사 2개를 조인다. 그다음 뒤 커버를 끼운다.
조정: 백건은 우물 바닥에 스페이서를 넣는다(1 mm당 +1.81 g). 흑건은 텅스텐 퍼티를 꼬리에 붙이면 1 g당 +0.67 g, 앞 밑에 붙이면 1 g당 −1.07 g.
건반 1개 빼기: 뒤 커버를 벗기고, 백건이면 스톱 바 손나사를 푼다. 꼬리를 2 mm 들고 앞으로 3.5 mm 당긴 뒤 앞을 들어 꺼낸다. 공구가 필요 없다.
noise: Down-stop 1: the steel bar top hits the 3T tail stop felt, peak 23.8 N (white, 1 m/s). The felt is in front of the centre of percussion, so the pin is pushed into its notch.
Down-stop 2: the front plate hits the v3 front felt 0.5 mm later, 16.5 N (white, 1 m/s). Overtravel is 0.78 mm (white) / 1.55 mm (black) at 1 m/s.
Pivot: the pin hops 0.10 mm (white) / 0.17 mm (black) at 1 m/s and re-seats on 0.5T cloth. It does not hop at all on return (hook impulse is positive).
Return: the crossbar hits the v3 hook felt 3T with a first bounce of 0.82 / 1.08 mm, settled after 52 / 85 ms.
Spring (white only): always preloaded (0.48 N) and guided by the dia 6.6 well; grease against ringing.
Coupling play: none, because there is no separate hammer or lever. This removes the blog's release clatter at its source. The bar is epoxied, so it cannot rattle.
removed_vs_reference: vs grand action: removed the wippen, jack, hammer and shank, let-off, repetition lever, damper, capstan, backcheck, front-rail pin and balance-rail punching; the key leads became one steel bar in the tail
vs GHS/Casio: removed the separate hammer lever and its shaft, the key-hammer coupling slot (source of the play and clatter) and the rubber-dome switches

vs v3: removed the preloaded PETG leaf flexure (the creep risk), the spine rail, 4 clamp screws, 4 setscrews, 4 brass discs and the x-reference pin; the white and black combs became 12 individual keys
design.self_assessment: Everything reported comes from calc.py: box-by-box mass and inertia with parallel-axis terms, gravity and spring torques as functions of angle, friction at pin, tab and fin, and a 2-DOF RK4 simulation that lets the pin lift out of its notch, with felt and notch contacts. In-frame S1 meets DW 47-55, UW >= 20, re-trigger >= 13.3 Hz, full return < 60 ms, rest stress < 2 MPa, magnet travel >= 5 and gap >= 3, all at 212/410 depth. It is weak where a short seesaw is inherently weak. The front/back ratio is 2.60. White inertia is low (19.4 g) and black keys feel different (42.7 g). It needs 9.0 kg of steel, and the white keys only get to 50 g with a helper spring (gravity share 48 %). The sweep in [11] and [12] shows no pin position inside 212 that fixes all three. The v2.0 claim of a ~40 ms full gravity return is confirmed at 39.4 ms, but re-triggering at 40 % rise gives 20 Hz. Uncertain inputs: felt stiffness (E 1.0 MPa nominal; sensitivity at 0.5, 2.0 and 2.5 MPa is checked), bushing preload, the stock spring's actual k, and the flat-bar, pin, thumb-screw and blade prices (estimates). The spring pack price is only verified as a range. If portability or piano-like inertia matters more than simplicity, S1 is likely beaten by a hammer-lever concept; S1's advantage is having no coupling play and the fewest moving parts.
stage0_tests: Print 1 white key, 1 black key and a 3-key-wide frame coupon (balance rail and fins, v3 hook/tab, front felt rail, rear wall stub with the tail stop bar). Fit a bar, pin and spring. Measure DW/UW with coins at y13, y62.5 and y90. Reject if DW is outside 45-55 g, UW is under 30 g, or y90/y13 is over 2.8.
Film the return at 240 fps. Reject if full return is over 35 ms (white) or 50 ms (black), or if the 40 % rise takes over 37 ms (under 13.3 Hz re-trigger).
Play fast forte 16ths on the coupon and listen at the pivot. If a tick is audible at mf, add a 0.1 mm-clearance retaining lip to the fin notch or use a harder tail felt, then retest.
Measure the spring k with 50 g and 100 g weights and set the white well depth (+1.81 g DW per mm).
Hand-cut 5 bars to time the 88-cut job and check how square the cuts are.
v3_interface_changes: The leaf combs (white and black) become 12 individual keys 206.5 long. The spine rail, clamp screws/nuts, setscrews, brass discs and x-pin are removed.
Add a balance rail y135-145 (top z21.5) with 12 fins 2.0 thick (top z27.0, notch at y140) and a USB tunnel x71-80 z5-10.5.
Add a tail stop bar (y186-209, z51.28-56.2) with a 3T felt strip and 7 spring pockets. It fits into a groove in the rear-wall top lip and is held by 2 M3 thumb screws.

The control board moves from y145.5-195.5 to y94-133 (stripboard cut to 39x70, components <= z15, 4067 on short pins). The ribbon from the sensor bar is 16 mm. The RP2040-Zero USB-C uses a 90 degree plug, a floor lane x71-80, and a rear-wall opening x71-81 z5-12 (was x74-94 z5-21).
The white front felt rail is re-sloped from 3.35 to 4.08 deg (felt top z13.24 @ y3.29 to z13.80 @ y11.09). The black stop rail goes from 4.62 to 6.13 deg (z13.70 @ y53.55 to z14.38 @ y59.85).
The rear cover front plate bottom goes from z44.5 to z46.5. The black raised top ends at y144.
Unchanged: sensor bar and element row y67, magnet positions, hooks and tabs, dovetails, frame depth 212, total depth 410, width 1254.

errors.issue: Body/tail transition at y146 collides. Each key's body/boss ends at y146 at its v3 x position, and each tail starts at y146 on the uniform 13.708 grid. In 5 of the 12 pairs a body and the neighbour's tail overlap in x (C|C# 0.15, D|D# 0.81, E|F 0.96, F|F# 0.97, G|G# 0.48 mm) with zero y gap. Pressing the tail's owner drives its tail front face forward into the neighbour's boss by 1.19 mm (white) or 1.66 mm (black). Pressing the boss's owner moves its boss face back 0.23 mm. The keys jam or drag each other. calc.py has no x model, so it never checks this.
errors.fix: Add a neck at y146-149.5 whose x range is the intersection of the key's body and its tail slot, with its underside at z>=23.5. Start the tail box (walls, keel) at y>=149.5, which leaves a y gap of 3.5 mm or more to every neighbour. The white bar then starts at y151 (47 mm, about 106 g), so re-solve the spring preload (about 0.52 N).

errors.issue: The install/removal procedure does not work. The keel front face (y146, down to z11 white / z9.01 black) sits 1.0 mm behind the balance rail rear face (y145, top z21.5). The key can slide forward only 1.0 mm (0.4 after FDM tolerance), but it must slide 3.5 mm to clear the 2.5 mm crossbar/hook overlap. Lifting the keel over the rail needs 11-13 mm of tail lift, which would hit the stop bar. So every key (black too) would need the stop bar off, plus an awkward tilt.
errors.fix: The same neck fixes it: with the keel starting at y149.5 there is 4.5 mm of forward travel with the pin raised 1.5 mm onto the lead-in flat. Black tails then rise only about 2 mm and can come out with the stop bar in place; white keys still need it removed because of the springs.

errors.issue: The first down-stop sits on a floppy mount. The tail stop bar is cantilevered from the 3 mm PETG rear wall (164 x 51.5, free-standing now that the spine rail is gone). The key-impact couple bends that wall across its layers: 43 N/mm at the felt line, in series with the 36 N/mm felt. One forte key moves the felt line about 0.56 mm; a 5-key chord moves it about 2.8 mm and pushes the wall top back about 4 mm, against 1 mm between the cover skirt and the rear bar. Pin lift roughly doubles to triples (black 0.31-0.41 mm at 1 m/s, 0.8-1.04 mm at 2 m/s, against a notch 1.5 mm deep). The front felt ends up carrying the stop, and front-felt-only stopping throws the pin out (1.6-9.5 mm in the sim). Wall bending stress is 8.8-12.4 MPa per chord, across layers. Also, below about 3.4 N finger force the static load goes entirely to the tail stop, not the front felt as claimed.
errors.fix: Shorten the tails 4-5 mm and make the rear wall 7 mm thick, or boxed (two 1.2 mm skins 6 mm apart). That gives 548 N/mm, and at 1.5 m/s the lift drops to 0.26 / 0.36 mm. Rebalance the bars and move the spring well to about y197.5. Alternatively, capture the pin with a cloth-lined retaining lip and let the v3 front felt be the only down-stop. Re-run the impact sim with the mount compliance included. The stage-0 coupon must use a full-width 3 mm rear wall, not a stub.

errors.issue: The v3 rear dovetails were kept unchanged (z3-17, female ceiling z17.3, y198-207, 4 mm deep at each seam). They now sit inside the C and B tails, whose keels are at z11 over y146-206.5. In v3 the spine rail filled this space, so it was never checked.
errors.fix: Move the rear dovetails into the solid balance-rail block (y135-145, z5-21.5), or cut them down to z3-9.5 under the white keel. Apply the same to the end parts.

errors.issue: The tail stop felt is angled at the white dip angle (4.08 deg), but black bars arrive at 6.13 deg. Black keys bottom on the felt's rear edge at 5.99-6.02 deg, so the black dip is 9.29-9.34 mm (spec 9.5) and magnet travel 7.9 instead of 8.07. The line contact on the felt edge will also wear it and change the dip.
errors.fix: Use a stepped stop: separate black felt pads (or shims) angled at 6.13 deg over each black slot, or re-level the black keel about 0.2 mm lower.

errors.issue: The 'printed top-face down, no supports' claim is wrong. White tail walls and bar pocket top out at z44.2, 0.7 mm above the key top plane (z43.5), so the head floats. Black tails (y146-206.5) top out at z42.21, 13.3 mm below the black top (z55.5) that sits on the bed, so the whole tail needs support.
errors.fix: End the white tail walls at z43.5 and let the bar stand 0.7 mm proud. Print black keys with tree supports under the tail (about +4 g and +0.3 h per key, about +150 g and +9 h for 88 keys), or print them on their side.

errors.issue: The helper spring is too slender: L0/D = 8.9, critical deflection 7.7 mm (fixed ends) against 13.35-17.82 mm working deflection. It buckles onto the well wall. The well mouth also shifts 1.38 mm and tilts 4.08 deg relative to the fixed pocket. Radial clearance is 0.3 mm, about 0.1 as printed. Expect scraping noise, PETG wear and 0.7-1.9 g of unmodelled hysteresis. The d0.4xOD6xL50 spring is not a verified stock item; the nearest stock part (0.6 wire) is about 6x stiffer and would raise the DW at the bottom to about 98 g.
errors.fix: Use a short spring guided on a steel pin fixed in the stop bar (L0/D <= 4, e.g. OD 6, L0 about 22-25, with k chosen so the rise from rest to bottom stays under about 10 g), or a steel leaf/torsion spring. Buy and measure the actual part before fixing well depths.

errors.issue: Black tail rear corner is 0.96 mm from the rear wall at full dip (0.36 after +-0.3 FDM on both parts), below the 1.0 mm rule.
errors.fix: Chamfer the black keel's rear-lower corner by 1 mm, or shorten the black tail 0.5 mm. Tail shortening for the thicker wall fixes this anyway.

errors.issue: The reported minimum clearance of 0.74 mm (black raised top to cover underside) is not a real clearance: the raised part ends at y144, in front of the cover plate at y146, and moves forward when pressed. The real minimum clearances (interference at y146, 0.96 at the rear wall) were missed.
errors.fix: Report clearances from a swept x-y-z check of neighbouring keys, not per-key z only.

errors.issue: The v3 rear-cover support posts (4x4 at (20,202) and (144,202)) now sit inside the C# and A# tails.
errors.fix: Delete them; the cover top can rest on the stop bar (0.3 mm gap).

errors.issue: There is no path shown for the RP2040-Zero USB-C plug. The v3 right-angle plug envelope (7.5 x 12.5, z9.45-16.95) at the board's rear edge (y133) has only 2 mm before the balance rail (y135). The rail/rear-wall lane is z5-10.5, lower than the plug body.

design.architecture: Rear-pivot printed key on a Ø3 SUS304 rod at (y171, z40), which is exactly v3's leaf instantaneous centre, so everything in front of y146 (sensor bar, magnets, front felts, tab+hook) is unchanged. A separate printed hammer pivots on a second Ø3 rod at (127.55, 15). A lug hangs from each key (black y96, white y108) and rests on a 14°-tilted felt pad on the hammer nose. This is a one-sided contact preloaded by gravity (1.51 N white / 0.86 N black), so the coupling has zero play. The lug positions make the white and black keys turn the same hammer by the same 10.43°, so all 12 hammers are one part. The steel weight is a cut piece of 9x25 flat bar (white 24 mm / 42.4 g, black 22 mm on a 2 mm shim / 38.9 g). It sits on the hammer's rear arm BEHIND the key rod (y182–207), over the shrunk control board and a felt ledge. The rest position is v3's tab hook felt, with the hammer holding the key up against it. Down-stop is v3's front felt. Hammer over-travel stop is a 3T felt strip under a printed stop rail on the rear wall. No spring in the base design; an optional soft assist spring can sit in the stop rail. The sensor reads the key magnet at y67 (v3 electronics kept).
design.summary_ko: 건반 뒤끝을 쇠막대 축(y171)에 걸고, 건반 밑 해머 레버의 뒤쪽 끝에 평철 조각 추(약 40 g)를 달아 추의 무게로 건반이 돌아오게 했습니다. 추를 건반 밑이 아니라 건반 축 뒤에 두었기 때문에 건반 높이(z43.5)와 센서·앞쪽 구조는 v3와 똑같습니다. 늘 휘어 있는 플라스틱이 없어서 오래 둬도 처지지 않습니다(정지 응력 최대 0.53 MPa). 계산 결과 백건은 누르는 힘 47.7 g, 올라오는 힘 35.6 g, 관성 질량 92.5 g으로 보급형 해머 건반(GHS급) 느낌이고, 흑건은 51.0 g입니다. 대신 추가 오르내릴 높이가 필요해 뒤 커버가 v3보다 7 mm 높아집니다(z66). 손을 뗀 뒤 완전히 돌아오는 데 61–64 ms가 걸리고, 가볍게(1.5 N) 연타하면 초당 12번으로 목표 13.3번에 조금 못 미칩니다(2 N이면 14.4번). 스프링은 필요 없다고 판단했고, 옥타브당 출력물 34개·구매 부품 19개, 추가 비용은 약 4.5만 원입니다.
design.how_it_works_ko: 건반을 누르면 건반 밑에 달린 둥근 돌기(러그)가 해머 앞쪽 펠트 패드를 눌러 해머가 약 10도 돌고, 뒤쪽의 강철 추가 12 mm 들립니다. 손을 떼면 추가 내려오면서 해머가 러그를 밀어 올려 건반이 제자리로 돌아오고, 건반은 v3와 같은 가이드 탭의 훅 펠트에 닿아 멈춥니다. 해머 무게가 늘 러그를 누르고 있어서 둘 사이에 헐거운 틈이 없습니다. 그래서 블로그에서 말한, 뗄 때 나는 '덜걱' 소리가 생기지 않습니다(복귀 시뮬레이션에서 틈 0 mm). 세게 치면 추가 스톱 레일 밑 펠트에 부딪혀 멈추고, 이때 러그와 패드는 0.2–0.4 mm만 떨어졌다가 펠트 위로 다시 내려앉습니다. 흰 건반과 검은 건반은 러그 위치를 달리해 같은 해머를 똑같은 각도로 돌리므로 해머는 한 종류만 뽑으면 됩니다.

risks: Lug/pad sliding (1.5 mm white, 2.2 mm black per stroke) makes pad friction the main friction term; mu is uncertain. At mu 0.10/0.25/0.35 the white DW is 46.3/50.5/53.3 g and UW 37.1/32.6/29.5 g. Pad felt wear over 10^6 strokes is untested.

The rear cover must rise from z59 to z66 (+7 mm): with the board under the weights, the weight's vertical room sets the achievable DW (same geometry at cover z59 gives DW 30.4 g). Alternative H1-B (key rod y164, 9x32 bar) needs only z61 but shortens the key lever (F90/F13 2.04).

Repetition is gravity-limited: 12.0 Hz (white) at a 1.5 N finger force, 14.4 Hz at 2.0 N; 13.3 Hz needs about 1.75 N. Even m_eff 75 g (cover z71) reaches only 12.9 Hz at 1.5 N. The assist spring does not raise the rate.
Full return is 63.6 ms white / 60.8 ms black, just above the 'ideally < 60 ms' goal; the optional spring gives 56.4 / 53.8 ms but adds +21 g near the bottom.
Stop rail takes 50 N (ff) to 70 N (10 N strike) per hammer, 6.1-8.6 MPa transient bending in a 5 mm PETG cantilever; fatigue and chord loads need a test.
Hammer yaw play +/-0.84 mm at the weight leaves a worst-case 0.94 mm between neighbouring rings; rubbing would be audible.
88 flat-bar cuts (hacksaw) and press-fit + epoxy quality; a loose block would rattle.
The hook felt carries 0.77 N constantly (white), so long-term felt set can raise the key front slightly (as in v3).
Felt stiffness model (E0 0.5 MPa) is back-calculated from v3's own estimate, so stop compressions and impact forces are +/- 50 %.
Frame gram estimate starts from v3's 175 g with estimated removals/additions; flat-bar price is unverified.
removed_vs_reference: vs grand action: hammer shank, jack/escapement, let-off, repetition lever, backcheck, dampers, capstan screw, balance pin and punching, front rail pin. Only the key plus one weighted lever and two steel rods remain.

vs Casio PX-720 / Yamaha GHS: rubber-dome switches (hall sensor reads the key), the captured lug slot that rattles (replaced by a one-sided felt pad preloaded by the hammer's weight), metal chassis, sponge under the weight (the weight floats at rest; the ledge felt is used only when a key is removed).
vs v3: leaf flexure, spine, spine rail, set screws, M3x40 clamps, brass discs, back stop rail (second floor). No plastic part is permanently bent: rest stress drops from about 6 MPa to 0.53 MPa max.

vs repo method D: the weight sits behind the key rod instead of rising into the key, so the key top stays z43.5 (D: z58). No hammer magnet (the v3 key-magnet sensing is kept). Filament 4.8 kg vs 7.6 kg. One hammer part for both colours.
noise: Key down-stop: v3 front felt 3T; pp 0.10 mm / 4 N, ff (6 N finger) 0.35 mm / 15 N.

Weight over-travel: block top (full 9x25 face) into the stop-rail felt 3T; ff 0.87 mm / 50 N, 10 N strike 1.10 mm / 70 N. This is the loudest impact, like GHS's hammer stop, damped by a thick felt over a large area.
Coupling after a hard blow: lug and pad separate only 0.21-0.42 mm and re-land on the 1T pad felt (graphite dusted).
Release: key crossbar into the hook felt 3T with 3.9 mJ (v3 design point 4.8 mJ); rebound 0.67 mm; lug/pad gap stays 0.000 mm, so there is no double 'deolgeok'.
Coupling play: 0 (one-sided contact preloaded 1.51 N white / 0.86 N black), no slot.
Pivots: steel rod in PETG slots with PTFE grease; the pad pushes the key backward onto its rod throughout the stroke (0.37 -> 0.10 N), so the slot does not click back and forth.
Lateral: hammer yaw +/-0.84 mm, worst gap 0.94 mm between rings (risk of rub).
Weight onto the ledge felt 1T: only when a key is taken out.

design.self_assessment:
Met: DW 47.7 / 51.0 g, UW 35.6 / 40.4 g, m_eff 92.5 / 95.0 g (GHS class), max rest stress 0.53 MPa (no creep path), sensor geometry identical to v3 (travel 6.12 / 8.46 mm, min gap 3.12 mm), frame depth 212, all moving clearances >= 1.06 mm, one hammer part for all keys, zero-play coupling that does not separate on release, +45k KRW, 4.8 kg filament (vs D 7.6 kg).

Not met:
- The cover cannot stay at z59 while keeping DW >= 47 g with a real stop rail. It needs z66; H1-B reaches z61 with a shorter key lever.
- Full return is 63.6 ms white, slightly over 60. The optional spring fixes this but adds a bottom bump.
- 13.3 Hz repetition needs a finger force of about 1.75 N; at 1.5 N it is 12.0 Hz. Shown to be a gravity/m_eff limit that neither a spring nor lower m_eff (down to 75 g) fixes.

All numbers come from calc.py. Its weakest inputs are the pad friction coefficient, the felt stiffness model, the frame gram estimate and the unverified flat-bar price. The 3-key coupon in stage 0 would confirm or falsify the concept within about two days.

errors.issue: Over-travel stop modelled as the full 9x25 block face under the felt, with a 0.5 mm gap at the face centre. At full dip the block and ring top is tilted 10.4 deg, so contact is the ring-back/rear edge (gap 0.89 mm). The 3T felt is crushed 66-77 % along a line, ff peak z57.8-57.9 comes within 0.6-0.7 mm of the PETG rail, lug separation is 0.55-0.93 mm, and repetition drops about 10 %.
errors.fix: Make the felt face parallel to the block top at the bottom position: tilt the rail or felt underside 10.4 deg, or chamfer the ring and block top so it is horizontal at full dip. Set the engagement gap at the real first-contact point. Use 4-5 mm felt, or felt over EVA, and re-run the strike simulation.

errors.issue: The weight rebounds off the stop and slams back onto the lug while the finger still holds the key. At 2 N hold, the key is kicked up 3-6 mm (34-72 % of magnet travel) after 6-10 N blows. This happens with the designer's own assumptions too. It can fire the 40 % firmware re-trigger (ghost notes). A lockout would overlap the 13.3 Hz window. The grand-action backcheck removed in 'removed_vs_reference' exists for exactly this.
errors.fix: Use a low-restitution stop (felt on a soft EVA or sorbothane layer, zeta >= 0.5 gives 1-2.7 mm), a catch that grabs the returning weight, or re-trigger logic that needs velocity reversal plus a minimum rise speed. Verify with 240 fps video of ff blows held lightly.

errors.issue: Stop-rail load path is not buildable. A 31 mm PETG plate is screwed with 3 M3s into the top edge of the 3 mm rear wall, which is too thin to tap. Each ff blow puts 7-10x the stop force into screw tension (280-650 N single, about 1460 N per screw for a 10-key chord) and bends the vertically printed wall across its layers (up to 24 MPa for a chord).
errors.fix: Build a stiff rear structure: an L-profile rail printed with a >= 8 mm rear wall, or an aluminium/steel angle (e.g. 20x20x2) bolted horizontally through the rear wall with nuts, loaded in bearing and shear rather than pull-out. This may cost +3 mm frame depth (bed still OK, rear-bar gap 3 -> 0 or total 413).

errors.issue: The 'weight floats 0.8 mm above the ledge' claim is false even in the designer's own model. Their rest angle (-0.01195 rad) puts the ring corner at z15.54, below the ledge felt at 15.70. Pad and hook felt compression is multiplied about 4x at the ring. The 1T pad felt is also crushed 73-86 % at every ff stroke, so it will pack. Result: the hammer rests on the ledge, lug preload is lost, the rest play and 'deolgeok' come back, and front heights drift about 0.5-1 mm.
errors.fix: Replace the pad felt with a hard low-friction slider (UHMW/PTFE tape on PETG, greased). Keep the hook at v3's front position (lever 158 vs 83.5). Give the ring at least 2-2.5 mm of rest gap, e.g. a lower or tilted ledge or a block 1-2 mm shorter (DW -2 to -4 g, recovered with putty or a lug at y109).

errors.issue: Several moving clearances are below 1.0 mm nominal (claimed min 1.06). Black key walls vs hammer-comb fin tops: 0.74 bottom / 0.27 ff (not checked by the designer). Black hammer nose vs v3 black tab base (y79-93, z5-12): 0.47 / 0.32. Black key rear-bottom corner vs key-comb fins: 0.66 / 0.51. Ring back vs rear wall: 0.90-0.95. Ring-ring lateral: 0.60 (yaw lever 80 mm, not 67). Rear arm vs own key-comb fins, lateral: 0.61-0.73. After +/-0.3 FDM tolerance several reach about 0.
errors.fix: Relieve the black key wall bottoms by 2 mm over y115-140. Trim the black tab base to y <= 91, or start the nose at y95. End the key bodies at y161 or chamfer the lower rear corner. Lengthen the hammer boss or tighten the fin fit to cut yaw. Narrow the ring/block (e.g. 8 mm steel) or stagger rings. Move the fins or narrow the arm to 5 mm.

errors.issue: The key is held forward (-y) only by a 2-5 N snap on a rear-open slot. Once pad friction is included, the pad pulls the key forward near the bottom: -0.9 N at mu 0.15, -2 to -3 N at mu 0.25, up to -5 N at mu 0.35, plus finger drag. Hard playing can unseat keys.
errors.fix: Add positive retention, e.g. a latch or keeper on the fin pair or the cover skirt engaging a notch in the tongue top, >= 15 N pull-out. Add a pull-out test at 10 N to stage 0.

errors.issue: The model and table put the up-stop hook and guide for BOTH colours at y84-91 and claim v3 is unchanged in front of y146. v3 actually has the white crossbar y10.5-14 under a hook at y11.5-14.5 (tab post y16.8-25, guide at the front) and the black crossbar y76.5-80 under a hook at y77.5-80.5. As drawn, the crossbar sits inside the tab post, which is impossible. With the real v3 positions, metrics change < 2 % and height error amplification is 1.08 instead of 2.05.
errors.fix: Model the real v3 hooks and tabs (as done here). Keep them. Update the coordinate table and the rest hook load (white about 0.41 N at y12.75).

errors.issue: The repetition claim is optimistic: 12.0/14.4 Hz becomes 10.8/12.9 Hz (white) at 1.5/2.0 N. 13.3 Hz needs about 2.1 N white, 1.9 N black.
errors.fix: Report corrected numbers. They improve once the stop is face-contact or dead; a 110 mm lug position or lower m_eff also helps.

errors.issue: The assembly sequence (insert both rods, then snap hammers from above) is impossible. The rear arm passes under the continuous key rod at y171, and the 10.6 mm ring cannot pass through its own key-comb fin pair (8.4 mm). Hammer removal is also not 'remove cover and rail, pull up': it needs all 12 keys out, the module detached and the key rod withdrawn.
errors.fix: Fit hammers before the key rod. Document hammer service as a module-level job, or split the key rod per key (short pins in fin pairs).

errors.issue: The steel block is held by a crush-rib press fit plus epoxy in a ring with no floor. That is a creeping preload (not in the 0.53 MPa claim), 5-min epoxy bonds PETG poorly, and the black shim has nothing under it.
errors.fix: Give the ring a 1 mm floor and a top snap lip or a through pin so the block is captured mechanically. Use epoxy only against rattle.

errors.issue: Rear cover z66 (+7 mm) is applied over the whole cover from y146. Only y >= 175 needs the height; ring front top at full dip is (176.5, ~52).
errors.fix: Step the cover: keep about z55-59 over y146-174 and rise only over the weights (y175-212).

interference: Black key side walls (x +/-4.3..5.5) vs hammer-comb fin tops (y118.5-136.5, z18.5, x +/-4.2..5.8): 0.74 mm at the nominal bottom, 0.27 mm at a 10 N blow (front felt 1.0 mm compressed). The designer never checked keys against the hammer fins.
Black hammer nose front face vs v3 black tab base (y79-93, z5-12): 0.47 mm at the bottom, 0.32 mm at ff over-travel. The designer modelled the tab as y84-91 without its base.
Black key rear-bottom corner (y163, z23.5; walls in line with the fins in x) vs key-comb fins (y165): 0.66 mm at the bottom, 0.51 mm at ff. White: 0.96-1.02 mm.
Ring back (y207.8) top vs 3T stop felt and PETG rail: first contact at a 0.89 mm gap; at a 10 N blow the felt is 77-79 % crushed and the ring is 0.62-0.69 mm from the PETG rail.
Ring back vs rear wall y209: 1.20 at hammer 0, 0.90 at the designer's rest angle, 0.95 with the hammer on the ledge.
At the actual rest state the ring and block bottom touch or sink into the ledge felt (designer's own rest: z15.54 vs felt z15.70). It is not 0.8 mm clear.
Lateral: neighbouring rings 0.60 mm (yaw +/-1.0 mm at y207.8). Rear arm vs its own key-comb fins 0.61-0.73 mm. Rear arm inside the black key channel 1.02 mm. About 0-0.4 mm after +/-0.3 tolerance.
Hammer rear arm is trapped under the continuous key rod at y171, and the ring cannot pass its own fin pair, so hammers cannot be installed or removed with the key rod in place.

As modelled by the designer, the white crossbar (y84-91, z23.5-25.1) lies inside the tab post (y84-91, z5-29.5). v3's real hook overhangs a crossbar in front of the post (white y11.5-14, black y77.5-80).
verify.notes:
I rebuilt everything independently in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kwg-Desktop-mydrive-project-Toccata/2f19e142-4ac2-4c90-bd1e-b3b469f97487/scratchpad/v4/verify/H1/verify_h1.py (own polygon mass model, circle-on-plane lug kinematics, force-balance DW/UW with pad/pin/guide friction, and a 2-DOF RK4 model with unilateral nonlinear felts). The stop felt is modelled as strips along the tilted block and ring top. Pad options are a Winkler cylinder or the designer's flat pad. Hooks are at v3's real positions. The designer's calc.py was not imported.

To check the solver, I ran it with the designer's assumptions (face-centre stop, flat pad, hook y87.5). It reproduces their results within about 1 %: 11.9/14.3/18.0 Hz, 46/67 N stop force, 0.33/0.36 mm separation.

What holds: statics, balance, m_eff, free-return times, sensor geometry, the single hammer part, steel mass, bed fit and rest stress. The architecture delivers GHS-class weight at 47-51 g DW with v3's front and sensing intact.

What fails:
- The over-travel stop is really an edge contact. It sits on a mounting that cannot carry the load.
- After a ff blow, the returning weight kicks a lightly held key 3-6 mm, enough to cross the 40 % re-trigger rise.
- The 0.8 mm rest gap is eaten by felt compression amplified about 4x. The weight already rests on the ledge in the designer's own rest state, so the zero-play claim does not survive felt set.
- Six clearances are below 1 mm; the minimum is 0.27 mm.
- Pad friction can pull keys off their 2-5 N snap.
- Repetition is about 10 % lower than claimed; 13.3 Hz needs about 2.1 N.

All of these are fixable inside the concept, so the verdict is fixable: a stop face parallel to the block at the bottom, a dead stop material or catch, a stiff rail anchor (L-profile or metal angle bolted in shear), a hard low-friction pad with >= 2 mm ledge gap, local reliefs for the listed clearances, positive key retention, and a hammers-before-rod assembly order. These may cost +1-3 mm height or depth and about +10-20k KRW, and should be re-simulated.

The optional assist spring was not re-checked.

design.name_ko: 뒤축 건반 + 강철 압축 스프링 + 관성 추 (부품 최소 기준안)
design.architecture: Single lever per key. Each key pivots at its rear end on one Ø5 S45C ground shaft per octave at (y200, z33.5). The key end is an open fork (slot 5.05, opening to the rear) held on the shaft by a Ø5x2 N35 magnet in the fork end (~2 N assumed), so a single key can be removed without tools. A steel music-wire compression spring stands on a printed guide post on the frame floor at y138 and pushes up on the underside of the key's top skin (white 0.45xOD5.5xL0 84.1, n40; black 0.45xOD5.0xL0 85.0, n75). Steel inertia mass is sealed inside the key by a print pause: white 16x16x34 SS400 square bar at y4-38 (68.3 g), black 6x19x47 flat bar on edge at y53-100, z33-52 (42.1 g). The spring preload carries the key's own weight, the steel's weight and the 47 g balance force, so DW = 50 g and the steel adds only inertia. The rest position is set by v3-style horizontal hook up-stops with 3T felt (white y42.5-45.5, black y104.25-107.25), and the dip is set by 3T front felt (white y3-12, black y51.5-58.7). v3 sensor bar, Hall row y67, control board, frame depth 212 and cover z59 are kept.
design.summary_ko: 건반마다 레버가 하나뿐인 가장 단순한 구조입니다. 건반 뒤끝이 강철 축에 걸려 돌고, 건반 속 스프링이 건반을 되돌리며, 건반 앞쪽 속에 넣은 강철 덩어리가 피아노 같은 묵직함(관성)을 줍니다. 계산 결과 백건 기준으로 누르기 시작하는 힘 50 g, 업웨이트 43.6 g, 앞끝 관성 65 g(손가락 위치 기준 75 g)이 나옵니다. 손을 떼면 바닥에서 40% 올라오는 데 33 ms, 끝까지 돌아오는 데 51 ms가 걸려 초당 17회 연타가 됩니다. 정지해 있을 때 플라스틱이 받는 힘은 최대 0.89 MPa라 v3처럼 휘어 처질 걱정이 없습니다. 대신 스프링 때문에 바닥으로 갈수록 힘이 조금 올라가고(백 59 g, 흑 62 g), 강철이 88건반에 5.3 kg 더해지며, 비용이 약 13.8만 원 늘어납니다.
design.how_it_works_ko: 건반은 뒤쪽 끝(앞에서 200 mm)의 강철 막대를 축으로 시소처럼 돌지만, 되돌리는 힘은 무게추가 아니라 건반 속 가는 강철 스프링에서 나옵니다. 스프링은 미리 많이 눌려 있어서 건반 자체 무게와 앞쪽 강철 무게를 떠받치고, 손끝에는 50 g만 남도록 맞춰져 있습니다. 그래서 강철은 손끝에서 무게로는 느껴지지 않고 움직이기 시작할 때 버티는 관성으로만 느껴집니다. 올라온 건반은 앞쪽 펠트 훅에 닿아 멈추고, 눌린 건반은 앞쪽 바닥 펠트에 닿아 멈추므로 모든 충돌이 펠트에서 일어납니다. 건반 뒤끝은 자석으로 축에 붙어 있어서 뒤 커버를 떼고 앞으로 3.5 mm 당기면 공구 없이 한 개씩 빠집니다.

errors.issue: The no-creep claim leaves out the frame. At rest each white key pushes the shaft up with 2.31 N (black 0.83 N) while its spring pushes the floor down at y138, so each module's frame carries a constant 20.3 N x 62 mm = 1257 N mm between the spring row and the fin comb. K1 removes the spine and rear-stop rails, so only the 2 mm floor carries it: about 11.5 MPa at y138 and 10.2 MPa at y145, and the bare floor would let the fin row lift about 7.5 mm. It will creep and change rest height and dip.
errors.fix: Add longitudinal webs from the spring row to the fin comb, for example 6 webs 2x20 mm outside the board x47-117 (my calc: 0.73 MPa), or move the board and add a box section. Also report the frame stress.

errors.issue: The re-trigger rate is overstated because the re-press is simulated from rest at the 40% point. In reality the key front is still rising at 0.24 m/s (white) / 0.32 m/s (black) there, and the finger must stop it first. At 150 gf the correct rate is 15.3 Hz (white) / 21.0 Hz (black) with ideal finger timing, and 12.6 / 17.0 Hz if the press starts when the sensor re-arms. The white key then misses 13.3 Hz. The claimed 17.3 / 23.9 Hz are not reachable.
errors.fix: Model the repetition with the key's velocity carried through (bang-bang timing, or press-at-re-arm). Report 15.3 / 21.0 Hz at 150 gf and 19.3 / 26.7 Hz at 300 gf. If margin is wanted, re-arm at about 30% rise.

errors.issue: The springs are slender and heavily preloaded: L0/D 16.7 / 18.7, deflected 57% / 43%. Buckling starts at about 3.5 / 2.8 mm of deflection (fixed-fixed), far below the working deflection. The Ø3.2 post (top z20 / z30) and 3 mm spigot leave 17.9 / 20.5 mm of coil unguided, and that section also buckles. The coil will bow into the key walls (radial room 3.2 / 1.8 mm), adding rub friction that is not in the model (a 5 gf rub gives white DW 52.2 / UW 41.2 g) and scraping noise. When a key is lifted out, the spring springs up to z89 and falls over.
errors.fix: Guide the spring over its full length: a Ø3 steel pin (or a printed sleeve) reaching about 1 mm below the spigot at dip (white about z33.5, black about z45.5). Use a larger OD (7-9 mm) for the white spring to lower L0/D, and grease it.

errors.issue: The fork and fin geometry does not fit together. With 13 fins 2 mm thick between 6 mm forks at 13.21-14.29 pitch, each fork can float 2.6-3.1 mm per side (calc.py hard-codes 0.30). The key can then yaw about its front guide: 1.65 mm sideways at y144, which exceeds the 1.354 mm white-tail to black-body gap. Neighbouring rear arms (gap 3.71) can also touch.
errors.fix: Size each fork to pitch - fin - 0.6, which is about 10.6-11.7 mm per key, or use thicker fins or spacer collars.

errors.issue: The fin between F and F# at x≈84 (z5-39.5, y195-205) sits in the path of the RP2040 USB-C plug (x77.75-90.25, z9.45-16.95, y195.5-220.5). Fins listed at y195 also overlap the control-board edge (y195.5) by 0.5 mm.
errors.fix: Arch that fin so z5-18 is clear, or merge F/F# into one wider fork gap. Start the fins at y196.

errors.issue: The install and removal procedure is wrong. The fork prongs run 6.5 mm behind the shaft's front face, so a key must start about 7 mm forward, not 3.5. A black key can move only about 1.5 mm forward before its front face (y51.5) hits the neighbouring white heads' notch faces (y50). It can therefore release neither its 2.5 mm hook overlap nor its fork, so black keys cannot be removed one at a time; both white neighbours must come out first.
errors.fix: Correct the slide distance to ≥7 mm for white keys. For black keys, change the retention: hook overlap ≤1 mm, or a vertical-drop up-stop, plus a fork held by a bar on the cover. Otherwise state that a black key comes out only after its white neighbours.

errors.issue: Only one Ø5x2 magnet stops the key moving forward. It sits behind a 0.7 mm PETG wall and pulls on a Ø5 round shaft, so 2 N is optimistic (likely 0.5-1.5 N). If the key creeps forward 2.5 mm, for example from a finger dragging toward the player, the crossbar leaves the hook and the 3.8 N spring throws the key front up.
errors.fix: Add a positive lock: a comb on the removable rear cover that drops into a notch on each rear arm, or a printed snap. Keep the magnet only for anti-rattle.

errors.issue: Print feasibility: the black key's rear arm top is at z43.5, 12 mm below its top face, so printed top-down it hangs over air for about 50 mm and needs support. The white fork (y196-204) overhangs past the arm skin, which ends at y196. The slot roof is a 6.5 mm cantilever.

verify.notes:
I rebuilt the model from scratch in my own box geometry, with the stated springs at their stated free lengths (not refitted). The core physics holds within 1-2%: masses and inertia, DW/UW, m_eff, return times to 40% rise and to full return, front/back ratio, magnet travel and gaps, spring forces and stresses, and up-stop impact energy.

The concept is fixable, not broken. One lever per key, with a preloaded spring carrying the steel's weight, gives DW 50 / UW 44 g, m_eff 65 / 37 g and full return 51 / 36 ms. None of the problems found needs a different architecture.

What is wrong:
- **Re-trigger rate.** calc.py sim_press re-presses from rest at the 40% point. The key front is still rising there at 0.24 m/s (white) / 0.32 m/s (black). Corrected at 150 gf: 15.3 / 21.0 Hz with best finger timing, 12.6 / 17.0 Hz if the press starts at re-arm; the claim was 17.3 / 23.9 Hz. I put the best-timing values in corrected_metrics. The white key meets 13.3 Hz only with good timing, or with about 300 gf.
- **Frame creep.** The no-creep claim covers only the key. The spring-to-shaft force loop puts about 1.26 N m per module on a bare 2 mm floor (about 11.5 MPa). Six 2x20 webs bring it to about 0.7 MPa. max_plastic_rest_stress_mpa = 11.5 is for the frame as drawn; key parts alone reach 1.23 MPa nominal, about 2 MPa at the step. v3's leaf loop likely had a similar, smaller floor moment (my rough estimate about 8 MPa), which v3 also never checked.
- **Spring buckling.** Not analysed beyond an acknowledgement; the guide post is too short.
- **Fork, fins and removal.** The fork/fin dimensions are inconsistent. One fin blocks the kept USB-C plug. The removal claim is false for black keys, the slide distance is wrong for white keys, and retention relies on an optimistic magnet.
- **Smaller issues.** Print overhangs on the black rear arm and white fork, a few clearances under 1.0 mm, and an inconsistent shim value.

**Checked and fine:**
- The finger point sits beyond the key's centre of percussion (white 173 mm from the pivot, finger at 187), so pivot reactions barely change on strikes. The fork's 0.05 mm slot play is therefore not a rattle source in normal playing.
- The spring never unloads, and there is no lever to separate from the key.
- Sensor gaps 4.70 / 4.90 mm and bar clearances 2.87 / 2.98 mm are fine.
- Depth 212 / 410, key tops z43.5 / 55.5, and the 220x220 bed fit are all fine.

m_eff of 65 g at the lip remains below the GHS-class aim of about 100 g, as the designer disclosed.

cost_delta_krw is kept at the designer's 138,191; the arithmetic checks, but the inputs are unverified.

design.architecture: Each key is a seesaw sitting by an open notch (R2.05) on a Ø4 SUS304 rod that lies in a printed balance rail (pivot y141, z21.5). The balance rail stands in front of the v3 control board, so the board, sensor bar, ribbon lane and USB tunnel all stay where they were. The visible key body is the v3 shape (y0-146, z23.5-43.5); under the cover it runs on as a solid 8x7 beam (z21.5-28.5) with a PETG capstan (R3, top z31). The capstan is at y188.32 on white keys and y180.61 on black keys. Behind the capstan the beam thins to 8x3 and carries a 1.5T felt pad that rests on a printed rear shelf (y196-209, z20). One weighted lever per key hangs on a Ø3 SUS304 rod at (203.5, 33.5): a printed carrier holding a 9x50x21.5 SS400 block (76 g) cut from 9T x 50 flat bar, with a 2T felt strip underneath. The lever lies on the capstan and is pressed onto it only by gravity (1.50 N white, 0.99 N black), so the coupling has no slot and no play. White and black levers are the same part. Rest is set by felt plus gravity: the lever holds the key tail down on the rear-shelf felt. Bottom is set by the v3 front felt 3T, and in the same instant the steel front-top corner meets a steel up-stop rail (3T x 19 with 2T felt, gap 0 +-0.3) held in 4 printed fins (x0.5/41.1/123.4/164.0, clear of the board). Return is pure gravity; there is no escapement, no repetition spring, no damper and no spring in the baseline. A +12 g bottom-assist spring and a heavier W1-S variant are computed as options. Black key fronts move 2.0 mm back and magnets move to y67. The rear cover rises from z59 to z73.2; J2 shows that z59 caps DW at 12 g for this architecture.
design.summary_ko: 건반은 Ø4 스테인리스 봉 위에 얹힌 짧은 시소입니다. 앞을 누르면 뒤 꼬리가 올라가 76 g 평철 블록이 달린 레버 하나를 들어 올리고, 손을 떼면 그 무게가 건반을 되돌립니다. 스프링 없이 다운웨이트 50.5 g, 업웨이트 43.6 g이 나옵니다(백 y13 기준, 흑 50.5/42.2 g). 재타건점까지 35.5 ms(14.1 Hz), 완전 복귀 55.8 ms로 목표를 넘고, 쉬는 동안 플라스틱에 걸리는 응력은 최대 0.71 MPa라 크리프 걱정이 없습니다. 대신 유효 질량은 65.8 g로 GHS(100 g 이상)보다 가볍고, 앞/뒤 힘 비는 2.52입니다. 옥타브당 강철이 0.91 kg(88건 6.7 kg) 늘고 뒤 커버를 z59에서 z73.2로 14 mm 올려야 합니다. z59를 지키면 이 구조로는 다운웨이트가 12 g밖에 안 나온다는 것을 계산으로 확인했습니다.
design.how_it_works_ko: 쉬는 동안 레버의 강철 무게가 건반 꼬리의 캡스턴을 1.5 N으로 누르고 있어서, 건반 앞이 들린 채 꼬리 끝 펠트가 뒤 선반에 얹혀 높이가 정해집니다. 건반을 누르면 건반이 4°, 레버가 12° 돌고, 강철 중심이 6.1 mm 올라가며 그 관성이 손가락에 약 66 g의 묵직함으로 느껴집니다. 바닥에서는 앞 펠트가 건반을 받고, 같은 순간 강철 앞 모서리가 강철 업스톱 레일의 펠트에 닿아 레버가 날아오르지 않게 막습니다. 손을 떼면 레버가 떨어지면서 캡스턴을 눌러 건반을 밀어 올립니다. 건반과 레버 사이에는 홈이 없고 항상 무게로 눌려 붙어 있어서, 블로그에서 말한 연결 홈의 '덜걱' 원인은 없습니다. 건반 밑의 자석은 v3 센서 바로 위를 5.2 mm(흑 8.0 mm) 움직여 세기를 잽니다.

risks: The rear cover rises from z59 to z73.2 (+14.2 mm) and the rear wall to z70.8. This is a visible change to a v3 interface: under z59 this architecture can reach only DW 12 g (J2), and moving the control board would still leave z64.3.
Adds 6.68 kg of steel for 88 keys (0.91 kg per octave; module about 1.52 kg). 88 blocks must be cut from 9T x 50 bar, by bandsaw or a paid cutting service.
Inertia at y13 is only 65.8 g (lip 54.2 g), below GHS-class 100 g+. More inertia breaks the 13.3 Hz / 60 ms return target unless the optional assist spring is added (W1-S: 81.4 g with +12 g spring).

After mf/ff strokes the heavy lever lifts 0.13-0.34 mm off the capstan (black fff 1.57 mm) and lands again at 0.12-0.60 m/s on 2T felt: a soft secondary knock, and the return after ff varies by phase (t40 11-36 ms).
Up-stop peak force is 36-62 N per key (ff/fff), so it must be a steel rail anchored in the fins. Its height tolerance of +-0.3 mm changes the lever flight (0.15-0.50 mm).
After a free return the key front dips again by about 22 % of the dip, because the lever bounces on the capstan felt. The rest-felt restitution barely changes this (H2).
The force curve falls from DW 50.5 to 45.4 g at the bottom (BW 47.1 -> 37.8) because the lever COM is 10 mm above its pivot.
Front/back ratio is 2.52 (v3 about 2.2) because the key pivot must sit at y141, in front of the control board.

The black key top slides 3.15 mm toward the player at dip (white lip 1.2 mm), because the pivot sits 34 mm below the black key top. To clear the white notch (1.18 mm) the black key front moves 2.0 mm back.
DW is sensitive to capstan position (1.51 g per 0.3 mm white). Per-key tuning with tungsten putty is expected.
All felt stiffness and restitution values (K, e) and friction coefficients are assumptions. Doubling friction gives DW 53.9, UW 40.2, t40 38.1 ms, full return 59.6 ms.
Keys are 12 separate parts per octave instead of 2 combs, so there are more prints and more assembly steps (27 printed parts per octave vs 5).

design.self_assessment: W1 meets the numeric targets without any spring: DW 50.5 / UW 43.6 g, re-trigger 14.1 Hz (white) and 16.0 Hz (black), full return 55.8 / 49.3 ms, rest stress 0.71 MPa, sensor gap at least 5.38 mm and moving clearance at least 1.18 mm. It also removes the slot rattle mechanism completely. Its costs are real, and calc.py confirms them: the cover rises 14 mm, it adds 6.7 kg of steel and 88 cuts, inertia is modest at 66 g, the front/back ratio is 2.52, the black key top slides 3.2 mm, and the heavy lever still bounces after ff (a soft felt knock). The dynamic numbers rest on assumed felt K, e and friction values, so the stage-0 tests decide. The heavier W1-S variant (81 g inertia, 56 g steel) is better only if the optional assist spring is accepted.
stage0_tests: Build a 3-key rig (1 white, 1 black, 1 spare) with printed frame section, Ø4/Ø3 rods and 2 cut steel blocks, then measure DW/UW at y13 and y64.5 with a coin scale. Calc gives 50.5/43.6 g white and 50.5/42.2 g black; more than 5 g off means the friction or mass model is wrong.
Film releases from the bottom at 240 fps: time to 40 % magnet rise and full return should be 35.5/55.8 ms (white). If t40 is over 37.6 ms the design misses 13.3 Hz without the spring.
Drop test the three felts (1.5T tail pad, 2T capstan strip, 2T up-stop) to get K and restitution e, then rerun calc.py with the measured values.

Record ff and fff strokes with a phone at 30 cm and compare the up-stop hit and the lever re-landing against the key-bottom felt; watch the high-speed video for lever lift-off (calc: 0.27 mm white ff).
Hold the rig at 60 °C for 2 h and check that the key rest height changes by less than 0.3 mm. This checks felt set and thin-tail creep at 0.7 MPa.
Play the black key at y64.5 and check whether the 3.15 mm forward slide of the black top feels acceptable; check the white-notch clearance at ff (calc 1.18 mm).

errors.issue: The up-stop rail is not held down. The fin slot runs z67.8-70.8 and the fins end at z70.8, so no material sits above the rail. Only the dust cover (snap arms) and gravity keep it in place, yet the rail takes 9.7 N (pp) to 60 N (fff) per key. Rail plus cover weigh 1.19 N. Unclamped, a single ff hit (about 50 mN s) would throw them about 9 mm, so the cover clatters on every note. A lip over the 19 mm front-open slot in a 1.6 mm fin cannot carry it either (about 1000 MPa for a 6-key chord). The claim that 'the rail is steel so the cover does not lift' is false. The optional assist springs also push up on the cover.
errors.fix: Bolt the rail down to local fin bosses at least 3 mm thick (M3 plus nut traps, 4 per module), or use closed slots with a lip at least 3 mm tall and raise the cover to about z76. Make the end fins at least 1.6 mm.

errors.issue: The key in its open notch has no hold-down, and calc.py pins the key to the rod, so it cannot see lift-off. The 4-DOF simulation shows each key hopping 0.08-0.13 mm off the rod at the end of every free return. Black keys also hop 0.08-0.21 mm when they hit bottom, because the front felt lies inside the black key's centre of percussion (93.5 mm vs 82-86 mm). The PETG notch then lands again on bare steel: a click, wear, and the key can walk in y. A 20 g upward pull at the key front, or tilting the module during transport, lifts any key off the rod. The front hooks were removed.
errors.fix: Line the notch with bushing cloth or PTFE, or make it a snap-over notch (about 200 deg wrap) that stays unloaded at rest, or add a hold-down strip 0.2 mm above the balance blocks. Keep the v3 front hook as a non-contacting keeper (0.5 mm gap).

errors.issue: The print plan leaves out supports. Printed top-down, the hidden beam, capstan and tail (y147-199) float 15-22 mm (white) or 27-34 mm (black) above the bed with nothing under them. The capstan crown, which slides on felt, becomes a supported surface. That raises friction, and doubled friction already drops the conservative re-trigger rate to 13.0 Hz.
errors.fix: Use tree supports under the beam (about 19 g per module) and sand the crown. Better: make the capstan an M3 button-head steel screw in a nut trap. That gives a smooth steel-on-felt contact and a per-key height adjustment for the up-stop gap.

errors.issue: The repetition margin depends on friction. 1/(2 t40) is 14.1-14.3 Hz nominal, but 13.0 Hz with full return 61 ms if friction doubles. The proposed assist spring (d0.30, OD6) has spring index C = 19, which is hard to make, and it pushes on the unclamped cover.
errors.fix: Design the spring mount into the baseline (the user allows springs), for example d0.35 OD6 with about 11 active coils (C 16). Decide at stage 0 from the measured friction. The spring needs the fixed cover or rail from error 1.

errors.issue: The felt contact law is misapplied. Lankarani-Nikravesh damping at nominal e = 0.35 gives an effective restitution of 0.69, so the reported 22 % rebound, the 0.12-0.60 m/s re-landing speeds and H2's finding that 'e hardly matters' are artifacts. The real rebound is 2-4 %.
errors.fix: Use a damping law valid at low e (Flores: chi = 8(1-e)/(5 e v0)), or fit K and e from the stage-0 drop test.

errors.issue: Clearances below 1.0 mm once the -0.3 mm FDM tolerance is applied. The lever hub-web top-rear corner comes within 0.75 mm of the rear wall at the white dip (not checked by the designer). The white key top vs cover curtain is 0.79 mm, because the curtain at y145-147 overlaps the key end at y146. Black front vs white notch is 1.18 mm, and black tail vs lever hub is 1.25 mm.
errors.fix: Round the web corner to R6 or end the web at y201. Move the curtain to y146.5-147.7, or its bottom to z45.5. Move the black front back 0.2 mm or enlarge the notch chamfer. Chamfer the tail end by 1 mm.

errors.issue: The balance-rail 'groove' has zero depth: the clearance calc puts the rail top at z19.5, which is the rod bottom. With a real 1 mm groove the balance block clears the rail by only 0.31-0.55 mm at the dip, so as drawn the rail does not locate the rod in y.
errors.fix: Add raised saddles only in the 5.7 mm gaps between balance blocks, or clip the rod at its ends and at the fins.

errors.issue: The 'gap 0' up-stop ignores the static set of the capstan felt under the lever's weight. At a slow dip the steel corner sits 0.41-0.54 mm below the up-stop (white) and 0.21-0.27 mm (black), which is outside the ±0.3 mm range studied.
errors.fix: Lower the rail by about 0.45 mm, or adjust per key with the capstan screw.

errors.issue: The key-removal numbers are wrong. The designer's own hub web meets the rear wall at about 16 deg, not 27 deg, leaving 4.3 mm of headroom at the capstan, not 7.2 mm. The procedure still works.
errors.fix: Correct the numbers, or trim the web.

errors.issue: Lever hubs abut, with only 0.2-0.7 mm slack per fin segment, so neighbouring levers rub on each other. Lever centres sit up to 2.3 mm off the key centres, so the F# and G# beams must jog outside their key width and the capstan load puts a 3.4 N mm roll moment on the key.
errors.fix: Leave 0.3 mm gaps or add washers. Place the fins at the E|F and B|C gaps. Jog the beams behind y147.

errors.issue: The rear shelf over the USB plug has a 27.4 mm unsupported 2 mm PETG span. Every F/F# return hits it with about 11 N, giving 8.9 MPa cyclic stress and 0.28 mm deflection toward a 1.05 mm gap: a fatigue risk.
errors.fix: Add two narrow ribs flanking the plug (about x76.5 and x91.5).

errors.issue: The cost is understated. The steel price is for a wholesale 6 m, 21 kg bar, and the 88 cuts (4-7 h by hacksaw) are not costed. The 1.5-3 mm steel corner striking the felt as a line contact (about 7 N/mm at fff) will cut and set the up-stop felt.
errors.fix: Budget about +27k KRW base plus the cutting option. Radius the steel's front-top corner or give it a printed or felt cap.

verify.notes:
I rebuilt the model independently (verify.py). It uses its own box masses, rigid-contact statics by virtual work, and a 4-DOF dynamic model: the key is a free planar body sitting in an open notch on the fixed Ø4 rod, and the lever turns on its rod, with felt contacts (Hunt-Crossley, Flores damping), Coulomb friction, key-lever separation and the up-stop. Scenarios: release from a settled bottom, pp-fff presses, and sensitivity runs.

The headline numbers hold. DW/UW, m_eff, front/back ratio, t40 and full return, magnet travel, rest stress and max z all agree within 2 % (friction within 21 %, from assumptions only). So the architecture meets the brief numerically without a spring, and is 'fixable', not 'broken'.

What the designer got wrong:
1. The up-stop rail is not retained against 10-60 N upward hits.
2. The open notch lets keys hop 0.1-0.2 mm off the bare steel rod every return, and black keys also hop at bottoming. The designer's pinned-key model cannot show this.
3. The key print plan omits supports under the floating beam and capstan.
4. The felt damping law is misapplied (effective e 0.69 vs the stated 0.35), so the reported 22 % rebound and the knock speeds are inflated.
5. Four clearances fall below 1.0 mm once the tolerance is applied. The worst are the lever web vs rear wall (0.75 mm) and the key top vs curtain (0.79 mm).
6. Smaller slips: the removal angle, the balance-rail groove, the up-stop nominal gap ignores felt set, hubs rubbing, fatigue of the shelf over the USB plug, and cost.

Repetition physics is handled correctly otherwise: the lever always stays on the key during the rise, because the key's centre of mass sits in front of the rod. The lever separates at the bottom and the up-stop takes its energy. The 1/(2 t40) rule is conservative. The margin is thin against friction, though: doubled friction gives 13.0 Hz. Because the user has said springs may be used ('필요하다면 스프링을 사용해도 좋아'), I recommend building the +12 g assist-spring mount into the baseline, with a C ≤ 16 spring, and reacting it on a bolted rail or cover.

Remaining architectural drawbacks (disclosed by the designer and confirmed here):
- The cover rises to z73.2. J2 confirmed: about 12.9 g DW is the maximum under z59.
- The front/back ratio is 2.52. That means 129 g at y90; v3's figure is 1.95, not 2.2.
- The black key top slides 3.2 mm, and its front moves 2 mm back.
- The force falls about 9 % toward the bottom.
- m_eff is 66 g.

Web price check: searches found only weight tables for flat bar (9x50 = 3.53 kg/m), not retail prices, so the cost correction is an estimate. Sources: [dystain flat-bar weight table](http://dystain.co.kr/layout/res/home.php?go=page2.2&mid=22), [onezaze cut-to-length flat bar](https://www.onezaze.com/goods/goods_view.php?goodsNo=1548), [changhojajae STS flat bar 4 m](http://www.changhojajae.com/m/product.html?branduid=470947), [dosomarket flat-bar spec note](https://dosomarket.com/knowledge/75).

design.architecture: Rigid printed key pivoting at its REAR end on a shared Ø3 steel rod (KP y205 z18, one per octave, held in a printed rear comb). Behind the visible key (y>146) the key continues only as a thin keel that runs low (z6-17) to a C-hook on that rod. In the dead space under the nameboard cover (y147-208, z13-57), each key has one printed counter-lever (a side plate carrying a 9x25 steel flat-bar piece: 40 mm for white keys, 37 mm for black). The levers pivot on a second shared Ø3 rod (LP y151 z35.8) that sits in open-top J-slots of 13 thin fin plates. The lever's short nose (r 10 mm white, 13 mm black; PETG R2) reaches forward into the key's hollow and pushes UP on a 0.6T cloth pad under the key skin at y141 (y138 for black). The contact is one-sided and gravity-preloaded, so it has no slot and no play. Pressing the key drives the nose down, and the steel rises about 0.8:1 with the key front. Releasing lets the steel fall and push the key back against the v3 front up-stop hook (felt). Rest = up-stop felt pressed by gravity only. A rear tab on each lever runs in a pocket of the rear comb between an upper overtravel felt and a lower rest-guard felt; the lever lands on the guard felt at the same time the key reaches its up-stop. The key stays at v3 height z43.5 with dip 10/9.5, and the v3 sensor bar and magnet are unchanged. The control board moves forward under the keys (y82-132).
design.summary_ko: 휘어서 버티는 v3 리프 대신 금속 봉 두 개와 중력만으로 움직이는 건반이다. 건반은 맨 뒤 강철봉에 걸려 돈다. 보이지 않는 이름판 커버 밑 빈 공간에 건반마다 평철 조각(흰 70.6 g, 검 65.4 g)을 실은 레버가 하나씩 있다. 계산상 흰건반 다운웨이트 53.5 g, 업웨이트 38.1 g, 유효 질량 71 g이다. 재타건 지점까지 36 ms(27.6 Hz), 완전 복귀는 58 ms이고 목표를 모두 넘는다. 건반 높이 z43.5, 딥, 센서, 프레임 깊이 212 mm는 v3 그대로이고, 제어 기판만 건반 앞쪽 아래로 옮긴다. 대가는 강철 약 6 kg과 부품 증가(옥타브당 출력 24개)다. 건반 하나를 빼려면 그 옥타브의 레버 세트를 먼저 들어내야 한다(공구 불필요). 기본 구성 비용은 약 +80,200원이다.
design.how_it_works_ko: 건반을 누르면 건반이 맨 뒤의 강철봉을 축으로 앞쪽이 내려간다. 건반 속 뒤끝(y141)에서 아래로 들어와 있던 레버의 짧은 코가 함께 눌리면, 레버가 자기 봉을 축으로 돌면서 뒤쪽 평철이 약 8 mm 올라간다. 손을 떼면 평철이 무게로 떨어지면서 코가 건반을 밀어 올리고, 건반은 앞의 펠트 업스톱에 닿아 멈춘다. 이때 레버 뒤 탭도 아래 펠트에 함께 내려앉는다. 쉬는 동안 건반을 붙잡는 힘은 평철의 무게뿐이다. 그래서 플라스틱이 계속 휘어 있는 곳이 없고(최대 1.46 MPa), 오래 두어도 무게감과 높이가 변하지 않는다. 코와 건반은 슬롯이 아니라 위아래로 눌린 한쪽 접촉이라 덜걱거릴 유격이 없고, 모든 멈춤 자리에는 펠트가 있다.

건반 12개: 자석을 CA로 붙이고 C훅 위 턱에 부싱 천 0.5T를 붙인다. 건반 앞을 1 mm 들고 제자리보다 4 mm 앞에 내려놓은 뒤 4 mm 뒤로 밀면, C훅이 건반 봉에 딸깍 걸리고 크로스바가 훅 아래로 들어간다. 레버가 없는 동안 건반은 앞 펠트에 눕는다.
레버 세트: 평철 조각을 캐리어에 끼우고 CA를 한 방울 떨어뜨린다. 레버 봉에 12개를 순서대로 꿴다(흰/검 레버 2종).
평철 쪽을 손으로 들어 코가 내려간 자세를 유지하고, 제자리보다 5 mm 앞에서 봉을 핀 J-슬롯에 내린 뒤 5 mm 뒤로 민다. 코가 건반 패드 아래로, 탭이 포켓으로 들어간다. 손을 놓으면 건반 12개가 업스톱까지 올라온다. 봉 고정 클립을 끼운다.
뒤 커버(윗판 1.5 구간)를 끼운다. 옥타브당 조립 부품은 출력 24개와 평철 12개, 봉 2개다.
한 건반 빼기(공구 없음): 뒤 커버 → 레버 세트를 5 mm 앞으로 당겨 든다 → 건반을 4 mm 앞으로 당겨 들어낸다. 용골이 평철 밑을 지나가므로 레버를 그대로 둔 채 건반만 빼는 것은 안 된다.
noise: Down-stop: v3 front felt 3T; peak 7-18 N for 0.1-1.0 m/s keystrokes

Lever overtravel: the rear tab hits the upper 3T felt (5x8) in the rear comb, 0.5 mm after the key bottoms. Peak 6 N at mf and about 50 N at ff; felt compressed 2.4 mm at ff. This is the largest impact, hidden at the back under the cover

Return: the key lands on the up-stop hook felt 3T while the lever tab lands on the guard felt (1.5 mm below rest), peak 3.5-4.2 N. Rebound 0.66 mm white / 0.57 mm black at the finger, settled within 0.2 mm after about 100 ms; ζ=0.5 felt gives 0.33 mm
Coupling: PETG R2 nose on 0.6T cloth, one-sided and gravity-preloaded, zero play. Lift-off only at the bottom, at most 0.43 mm, relanding at up to 0.37 m/s on cloth. No slot, so no 'deolgeok' rattle
Key rod C-hook: the lower jaw carries the load at rest (rod pushes the key down 1.1 N). The upper jaw sees up to +5.6 N only at the down-stop impact, so it is lined with 0.5T cloth and fitted snug

Thin keel (3-8 mm) at a constant 1.46 MPa, and keys need a designed breakaway rib when printed upside down

design.self_assessment: By the calc.py model every §6 numeric target is met without a spring: DW 53.5/49.5 g, UW 38 g, m_eff 71/67 g, re-trigger 27.6/28.5 Hz, full return 57.6/55.7 ms, rest stress 1.46 MPa, magnet gap >= 4.04 mm. Key height, dip, sensors, 212 mm frame and 410 mm total depth are kept. The v2.0 claim that gravity return is fixed at about 40 ms is shown to be wrong. The cost is real. The design adds about 6 kg of steel and 24 printed parts per octave. Individual key removal requires lifting the octave's lever set first. The control board has to move under the keys. The ff overtravel stop and the 0.37 mm black-key front clearance are the weakest margins. Friction coefficients and felt stiffness/damping are assumptions, not measurements. Steel and cable prices are estimates; only the Ø3 SUS rod price was checked. Stage 0 should measure DW/UW and the return on a single key before committing to 88.

errors.issue: The keel is modelled as rigid but is a soft spring. Tip compliance is 0.252 mm/N (k ≈ 4 N/mm). While the heavy lever accelerates, the rod carries about 2× the finger force, so the key's rear lifts 1.2 / 2.2 / 3.2 mm at 0.3 / 0.6 / 1.0 m/s. This invalidates the rigid 2-DOF dynamics and the claimed 'no plastic stress' story: dynamic keel stress is 6.5-17 MPa (compliant) or up to 37 MPa (rigid-model loads) on every forte stroke, against 1.46 MPa claimed at rest. That is a fatigue and fracture risk in a 4.5×7.5 PETG section.
errors.fix: Make the keel steel or steel-reinforced. For example, bond a 3×6 mm steel flat on edge (about 62 mm per key) into a slot along keel A/B, or form keel, riser and hook from one bent 3×6 strip fixed to the key web. Target ≤0.01 mm/N and PETG stress <5 MPa at 1 m/s. The fallback of a 10 mm wide, full-height PETG keel still gives 0.06 mm/N and 9-10 MPa at ff, which is marginal.

errors.issue: Keel to lever-carrier clearance was checked only at static rest (1.63 claimed, 1.36 / 1.21 recomputed). On every release the lever lands on its guard while the key presses into the up-stop felt, and the gap at y≈171.5 closes to 0.37 (white) / 0.16 (black) mm in the rigid model and to contact with the compliant keel. During strokes it is 0.33-0.79 mm. Expect a click or rub on every note.
errors.fix: Aim for ≥1.3 mm in every pose. Options: end the tall keel A at y≈165 and step down; reduce the guard drop from 1.5 to about 1.0 mm (with the shim adjustment already planned); a thinner steel keel frees about 3 mm. Re-check at rest, guard+up-stop, bottom and ff.

errors.issue: The rear stop tab (5×4 section on a 1.2 mm end wall) takes the whole ff overtravel impact: 25-58 N into a 5×8 3T felt at 74 % compression. Stress is 15-34 MPa (white) and 35-48 MPa (black, 11 mm arm), which is near PETG's 51 MPa. The same deceleration pulls the steel upward with 40-97 N, against only a press fit and a drop of CA in an open-top carrier.
errors.fix: Positively capture the steel with a Ø3 cross-pin through the bar and carrier, or a closed carrier lip. Make the overtravel stop act on a stout lever section: a tab of at least 6×8 gusseted to the side plate and floor, or strike the steel directly. Use at least about 100 mm² of felt (or 2 stacked layers, or Poron) so compression stays under 50 % at 1 m/s. This also keeps the steel top ≥1.3 mm under the cover at ff.

errors.issue: The black key front clears the white notch face by 0.36 mm nominal and 0.18 mm at ff with the white neighbour bouncing, which violates ≥1.0 mm. The rear pivot at z18 swings the black front forward by 1.6-2.3 mm. The added 2.5 mm chamfer does not help, because the collision zone is the vertical notch face at z40.9-43.5.
errors.fix: Move the white notch faces forward about 1.0-1.2 mm (visible gap 1.5 → 2.7 mm) or the black key fronts back by the same amount. Either gives ≥1.18 mm at ff.

errors.issue: The claim that the lever rod is always loaded downward is false. The overtravel tab sits beyond the lever's centre of percussion (52.8 vs 32 mm), so the pivot reaction reverses: the rod is lifted 3-5 N at 0.3 m/s and 14-38 N at 1 m/s. Open-top J-slots in fins that end at z38 leave at most about 0.67 mm over the rod, which means rattle at every mf/ff note and possibly a broken ceiling.
errors.fix: Raise the fins to about z44 with a J ceiling of 3 mm or more and a cloth lining. Alternatively capture the rod with a screwed cap strip or closed bores (the rod then slides in from the side, like the key rod).

errors.issue: Relocating the control board is incompletely designed. The Zero's +y USB-C plug (overmold about 12.5×7.5×25) would sit at y132-157, inside the fins and keel necks, and above the z14.5 cap. The new full-width rear comb (y200-209, z5-52) blocks the v3 USB tunnel at x74-94, the keels fill z6-17 at every column, and there is no cable route to the rear for USB or the O1/O7 EXT leads. The v3 floor windows at y96-136 lie under the new board. Black-key clearance to the board is 1.39 mm static and about 0.9 mm at ff.
errors.fix: Move the board to y95-145 (≥2.2 mm under pressed black keys) and close those floor windows. Turn the Zero's USB to −x with a right-angle low-profile cable run on the floor in the gap between two keels. Notch the two fins at z5-9 and cut a floor-level hole (about 13×8 at z5-13) through the rear comb and rear wall, so the female end sits in the cable passage.

errors.issue: The re-trigger rate is reported as 1/t40 (27.6 / 28.5 Hz), which leaves out the re-press. A real repeat cycle is 20.6-23.8 Hz. The 37.4 Hz protocol result depends on felt and upper-felt rebound, and becomes erratic (13-41 ms) once the keel compliance is included.
errors.fix: Report the cycle rate (t40 + re-press) as the metric. It still clears 13.3 Hz.

errors.issue: Other forte-stroke stresses and clearances were never checked. The white skin under the nose pad sees 2-12.5 MPa. The black nose arm (r 13, 3.6×5) sees up to 22 MPa. I rebuilt the model independently in verify.py without importing the designer's calc.py. It has its own box mass model, nose-contact kinematics, statics with friction, rigid 2-DOF and compliant 3-DOF dynamics (key angle, keel deflection, lever angle), felts, and a pressed-touch finger with k_f 5 and 10 N/mm.

**What holds.** All the static and gravity-return numbers reproduce within 1 %:
- DW / UW 53.5 / 38.2 g (white) and 49.5 / 38.7 g (black).
- m_eff 71.4 / 67.3 g; front/back ratio 1.67.
- t40 36.1 / 35.0 ms; full return 57.7 / 55.7 ms.
- Magnet travel 6.78 / 8.72 mm; magnetic gap 4.04 / 4.63 mm.
- Rest plastic stress 1.46 MPa; envelope 212 / 410 deep, key top z43.5.

The architecture meets the §6 targets on paper. Two caveats:
- DW rises to about 57 g if pivot μ is 0.3 or more, so grease the rods.
- Full return has only about 1 ms margin to 60 ms.

**What fails.** Everything the designer checked only at rest breaks under dynamic load:
1. **Keel.** It is not rigid (0.25 mm/N). It bends up to 3.2 mm and sees 17 MPa at 1 m/s (37 MPa with rigid-model loads). It also hits the lever carrier on every release, because the guard/landing pose was never checked against it.
2. **Tab and steel retention.** The black tab reaches 35-48 MPa at ff, and the open-top carrier must resist a 40-97 N steel pull-out.
3. **Lever rod.** It lifts out of its open J-slots at mf/ff, so the "no rattle" claim fails.
4. **Black front clearance.** 0.36 mm (0.18 at ff) against a 1.0 mm rule.
5. **Board and cable routing.** The relocated control board has no feasible USB/EXT route as drawn.
6. **Re-trigger metric.** It leaves out the re-press. The real cycle is about 21 Hz, which still passes.

**Verdict.** None of this defeats the architecture: steel keel strip, pinned steel, stout stop, a 1.2 mm notch shift, captured rod and re-packed board. With these fixes the concept should still meet the brief, at roughly +30-60k KRW and about 176 extra small steel parts. The steel and cutting prices could not be verified online; only 'from 5,500 KRW/m' cut-to-length listings were found (onezaze.com, metalmarket.co.kr), so the cost is plausible but likely low.

**Suggested stage-0 additions.**
- Measure the keel tip stiffness with a 1 kg hanging load. The model predicts about 2.5 mm deflection for the current keel.
- Film a ff stroke at 240 fps to catch keel-carrier contact.
- Do the 100 g drop test on a black key to check the tab.

건반 하나만 움직이는 가장 단순한 시소다. 프레임 212 mm, 커버 z59, v3 훅·센서를 그대로 쓰고 쉼 응력은 0.66 MPa다. 그러나 212 mm 안의 짧은 시소라는 한계가 숫자로 드러난다. 백건 복귀 힘의 52 %를 스프링이 내므로 요청한 중력 복귀가 아니다. 백건 m_eff는 19 g로 스프링 건반 수준이고 흑건 43 g와 느낌이 다르다. 앞/뒤 비는 2.6이고 강철은 9 kg(모듈 1.87 kg)으로 가장 무겁다. 검증에서 y146 건반 충돌(치명), 설치 불가, 3 mm 뒷벽에 얹힌 스톱(핀 들림 2~3배), 도브테일 간섭, 가는 스프링 좌굴이 나왔다. 모두 고칠 수는 있다.

건반당 레버 1개 + 스프링 1개로 커버 z59, 깊이 212를 지키는 가장 작은 안이고 앞/뒤 비 1.7도 좋다. 그러나 복귀 힘을 무게가 아니라 긴 압축 스프링이 전부 낸다(강철은 관성용). 그래서 사용자의 1순위(중력 복귀)와 다르다. 힘 곡선은 50→59/62 g로 스프링처럼 올라가고, UW 44 g는 튀는 느낌을 주며, 흑건 관성은 백건의 0.57배다. 검증에서 나온 문제: 스프링→축 하중 고리가 2 mm 바닥에 11.5 MPa를 늘 걸어 프레임 크리프, L0/D 17 스프링 좌굴, 포크·핀 치수 불일치, USB 간섭, 흑건 단독 분리 불가, 연타 15.3 Hz(주장 17.3). 맞춤 스프링 때문에 가장 비싸다(+13.8만 원, 미확인).

느낌 숫자가 가장 좋다. 앞/뒤 비 1.67, m_eff 71/67 g로 백·흑이 고르고, 실제 연타 주기로 약 21 Hz, 완전 복귀 58 ms이며 건반 높이와 커버 z59도 유지한다. 그러나 무게 레버 밑을 지나는 가는 PETG 용골이 실제로는 스프링이다(0.25 mm/N). 세게 칠 때마다 17~37 MPa(치명)를 받고, 흑건 뒤 탭은 35~48 MPa로 PETG 강도 51 MPa에 가깝다. 복귀 때 용골이 레버와 닿고, 레버 봉이 J-슬롯에서 들리며, 흑건 앞 틈은 0.36 mm다. 제어 기판을 옮겨 저높이로 다시 만들어야 하는데 USB 경로가 없다. 건반 하나를 빼려면 레버 세트를 먼저 들어내야 한다. 강철 용골 보강까지 넣으면 부품이 가장 많아진다.

사용자가 보여준 카시오 GIF와 가장 닮았다. m_eff 93/95 g(GHS급)로 관성은 가장 피아노답고, y146 앞은 v3 그대로이며, 강철이 3.7 kg로 가장 적고 싸다(+4.5만 원). 그러나 검증에서 결함이 가장 많이 나왔다. 오버트래블 스톱이 모서리로만 닿고, 그 레일은 3 mm 뒷벽에 M3로 박을 수 없다. ff 뒤 되튄 추가 가볍게 누른 건반을 3~6 mm 차올려(자석 이동의 34~72 %) 유령 재타건을 낼 수 있다. 추는 쉼 상태에서 이미 받침 펠트에 얹혀 예압을 잃고, 패드 펠트는 73~86 %까지 눌려 결합부 '덜걱' 유격이 되살아난다. 연타는 1.5 N에서 10.8 Hz로 목표 13.3 Hz에 못 미치고 완전 복귀는 64 ms다. 틈 6곳이 1 mm 미만(최소 0.27)이고 커버는 z66이다.

밸런스 레일 홈 깊이가 0으로 그려져 봉이 y로 고정되지 않는다. 밸런스 블록 사이 5.7 mm 틈에만 받침(새들)을 세우거나 봉 양끝·핀에서 클립으로 잡고, 블록↔레일 틈을 1 mm 이상으로 한다.
캡스턴 펠트가 정적으로 눌려(백 0.41~0.54, 흑 0.21~0.27 mm) 느린 딥에서 강철이 업스톱에 먼저 닿는다. 레일을 약 0.45 mm 내리거나 캡스턴 나사로 맞추는 절차를 조립 순서에 넣는다.
레버 허브가 맞닿아 서로 문지른다. 허브 사이에 0.3 mm 틈이나 와셔를 두고 핀은 E|F·B|C 틈에 둔다. 레버 중심과 건반 중심이 최대 2.3 mm 어긋나므로 F#·G# 빔은 y147 뒤에서 꺾고, 롤 모멘트 3.4 N·mm를 확인한다.
USB 플러그 위 뒤 선반의 27.4 mm 스팬은 F/F# 복귀마다 11 N을 받아 8.9 MPa 반복 응력과 0.28 mm 처짐이 생긴다(틈 1.05 mm). x76.5와 x91.5에 리브 2개를 넣는다.
건반 빼기 절차 숫자를 고친다: 레버는 16°까지만 젖혀지고 캡스턴 위 여유는 4.3 mm다(노치 2.05 mm를 들기에는 충분). 천 라이닝, 키퍼, 손나사 레일을 반영한 순서로 다시 쓴다.
비용 확인: 9T×50 평철 1.4만 원은 6 m 도매(21 kg, 택배 불가) 가격이다. 소량 절단 판매 가격, 강철 약 7.6 kg 배송비, 88회 절단(손톱 4~7시간 또는 외주 4.4만~8.8만 원)을 확인한다. 이식 부품(캡스턴 나사·너트 24, 손나사 4, 부싱 천)을 더해 약 +3.5만 원으로 다시 잡는다.
느낌 판정 항목(단계 0 시편으로 결정): 앞/뒤 비 2.52(y90 129 g, v3 실제 1.95), 흑건 윗면이 딥에서 3.2 mm 연주자 쪽으로 미끄러지는 것, 바닥으로 갈수록 DW가 약 9 % 줄어드는 것을 직접 쳐 보고 받아들일지 정한다. 받아들일 수 없으면 W1-B(기판 이동 + 피벗 y160)로 간다.
외곽과 운반: 커버 z73.2는 뒷바(가운데 유닛 약 z122)보다 낮지만 스피커 배플, 케이블 통로와의 관계를 도면에 표시한다. 모듈 무게 약 1.52 kg(v3 0.59)을 R18 운반 기준으로 다시 적는다. v3 커버 받침 기둥(척추 위 (20,202)·(144,202))은 척추가 없어지므로 커버를 핀·레일 위에 얹는다.
judge.recommended_design_ko:
권장안: W1+ — 짧은 시소 건반 + 꼬리가 들어 올리는 무게 레버(이식 반영)

[원리]
건반은 Ø4 SUS304 봉 위에 얹힌 시소다(피벗 y141, z21.5). 앞을 누르면 건반 꼬리의 강철 캡스턴이 올라가 뒤쪽 무게 레버를 들고, 손을 떼면 레버의 평철 무게(76 g)가 캡스턴을 눌러 건반을 되돌린다. 기본 구성에는 스프링이 없어 중력만으로 돌아오고, 쉼 위치도 '레버 무게 + 뒤 선반 펠트'가 정한다. 늘 휘어 있는 플라스틱은 없다(쉼 응력 최대 0.72 MPa). 건반과 레버는 홈 없이 무게로 눌려 붙어 있는 한쪽 접촉이라, 블로그에서 말한 연결부 '덜걱' 유격이 없다.

[부품, 옥타브당]
- 출력(27개): 건반 12(한 개씩, 보이는 모양은 v3 y0~146, z23.5~43.5), 레버 캐리어 12(백·흑 공통 1종), 프레임 1(밸런스 레일 y137~145 + 뒤 선반 y196~209 z18~20 + USB 옆 리브 2 + 핀 4장 x0.5/41.1/123.4/164.0 + 높인 뒷벽), v3 센서 바 1, 먼지 커버 1.
- 구매: SS400 평철 9T×50을 21.5 mm로 자른 조각 12(각 76 g, 캐리어 립·핀으로 가둠), Ø4 SUS304 건반 봉 1, Ø3 SUS304 레버 봉 1, 강철 업스톱 레일 3T×19×163 1(밑면 펠트 2T, 흑 칸 1.8 mm 패드), M3 버튼헤드 캡스턴 나사 + 너트 12조, M3 손나사 4, 자석 Ø5×2 12(v3), 부싱 천 0.5T(노치), 펠트(꼬리 1.5T, 레버 밑 2T, v3 앞 3T).
- 옵션 자리: 레일에 보조 스프링용 Ø2 가이드 핀과 포켓(W1-S). 스프링은 단계 0 결과를 보고 끼운다.

[위치와 동작]
- 건반 피벗: Ø4 봉 (y141, z21.5). 봉은 밸런스 레일의 새들 위에 있고, 노치는 R2.55에 천 0.5T를 댄다.
- 캡스턴(M3 강철 나사, 머리 z31): 백 y188.3, 흑 y180.6. 반 바퀴로 DW 약 1.3 g을 조정한다.
- 레버 피벗: Ø3 봉 (y203.5, z33.5). 강철은 쉼에서 y149~199, z33~54.5이고, 딥에서 앞 윗모서리가 백 z65.7, 흑 z63.9까지 오른다.
- 쉼: 레버가 캡스턴을 1.50 N(흑 0.99 N)으로 눌러 꼬리 끝 1.5T 펠트가 뒤 선반에 앉는다. v3 앞 훅은 크로스바에서 0.5 mm 떨어진 '닿지 않는 키퍼'로만 남긴다.
- 바닥: v3 앞 펠트 3T가 건반을 받고, 같은 순간 강철 앞 윗모서리(둥글림, 캡)가 손나사로 고정한 강철 업스톱 레일의 펠트에 닿는다(흑 칸은 1.8 mm 패드로 높이를 맞춤).
- 센서: 자석을 y67로 옮긴다. 이동 5.22 / 7.97 mm, 최소 간격 5.60 / 5.38 mm(ff 4.89).
- 제어 기판, 리본, USB는 v3 자리 그대로다(부품 z20 이하).
- 외곽: 프레임 깊이 212, 전체 1254×410은 그대로이고 커버만 z59에서 z73.2로 오른다. 커버는 뒷바(가운데 유닛 약 z122)보다 낮아 전체 윤곽 안에 있다.

[성능, 독립 검증값]
- 백 y13: DW 51.2 g / UW 42.8 g, 마찰 4.2 g. 흑: 51.4 / 41.2 g.
- 유효 질량: 백 65.8 g, 흑 56.9 g.
- 복귀: 바닥에서 40 %까지 약 35 ms, 재타건 14.3 Hz(흑 16.2). 완전 복귀 55.7 / 49.3 ms. 보조 스프링을 끼우면 약 16 Hz.
- 앞/뒤 비 2.52(y90에서 129 g).
- 강철: 옥타브당 911 g, 88건반 6.7 kg(레일·봉 포함 7.6 kg). 모듈 약 1.5 kg.
- 출력: 필라멘트 약 5.6 kg, 371 h. 모든 부품이 220 베드에 들어간다.
- 비용: v3 대비 약 +3.5만 원(평철 절단 외주 시 +4.4만~8.8만 원), 100만 원 한도 안.

[건반 하나 빼기, 공구 없음]
커버를 들고, 손나사를 풀어 업스톱 레일을 앞으로 빼고, 그 레버를 16° 젖힌다(캡스턴 위 4.3 mm 여유). 건반 앞을 살짝 들어 키퍼를 넘기고, 노치를 봉에서 떼어 앞으로 뺀다.

[뺀 것]
- v3: 리프 콤, 척추와 척추 레일, 클램프 나사, 세트스크루, 황동 원판, 두 번째 바닥 레일.
- 그랜드: 윕펜, 잭, 해머, 렙리션, 백체크, 댐퍼, 밸런스 핀 펀칭.
- GHS/카시오: 해머-건반 연결 슬롯(덜걱의 원인), 고무 돔, 추 밑 스펀지.

[단계 0]
3건반 시편(백·흑·백)을 v3 폭 프레임 조각, 실제 봉, 강철, 볼트 고정 레일로 만든다. 확인할 것:
- 저울로 y13 DW/UW, y90 힘.
- 240 fps 영상으로 t40과 완전 복귀.
- ff 뒤 가볍게 누른 상태에서 건반 들림.
- 펠트 낙하 시험으로 K·e.
- 60 °C 2시간 뒤 높이 변화.
- 앞/뒤 비와 흑건 미끄러짐을 직접 쳐 보고 받아들일지. 안 되면 W1-B(기판을 앞으로 옮기고 피벗을 y160으로, 비 약 2.1)로 간다.
judge.user_facing_comparison_ko:
다섯 안 모두 v3의 늘 휘어 있는 PETG 리프를 없앴습니다. 쉼 응력이 0.5~1.5 MPa로 떨어져 처짐 걱정은 사라졌고, 독립 검증에서 구조를 버려야 할 결함은 없었습니다(다섯 안 모두 '고칠 수 있음'). 아래 숫자는 설계자 주장이 아니라 검증값입니다.

1. W1 짧은 시소 + 무게 레버 — 추천(6.8점)
   - 스프링 없이 무게만으로 돌아옵니다. DW 51 / UW 43 g, 관성 66 g, 연타 14.3 Hz, 완전 복귀 56 ms.
   - 추가 비용 약 3만 원으로 가장 싸고, 제어 기판·센서·USB가 v3 자리 그대로입니다.
   - 대신 뒤 커버가 14 mm 높아지고(뒷바보다는 낮음), 검은 건반 사이(y90)를 누르면 129 g로 무겁습니다.

2. S1 미니 시소 — 차점(6.2점)
   - 움직이는 부품이 건반 하나뿐이고 커버 높이도 v3 그대로입니다.
   - 하지만 흰 건반은 복귀 힘의 절반을 스프링이 내고, 흰 건반 관성이 19 g라 스프링 건반 느낌에 가깝습니다.
   - 강철이 9 kg로 가장 무겁습니다.

3. K1 스프링 + 관성 추(6.1점)
   - 가장 작습니다(커버 z59).
   - 하지만 되돌리는 힘을 무게가 아니라 긴 스프링이 내서 요청하신 방향과 다르고, 바닥으로 갈수록 무거워집니다(50→59 g).
   - 맞춤 스프링 때문에 가장 비쌉니다(+13.8만 원).

4. F1 뒤쪽 무게 레버(5.8점)
   - 느낌 숫자가 가장 좋습니다(앞/뒤 비 1.67, 관성 71 g, 약 21 Hz, 커버 z59).
   - 하지만 추를 받치는 가는 플라스틱 용골이 칠 때마다 크게 휘어 강철 보강이 필요합니다.
   - 제어 기판을 새로 만들어야 하고, 건반 하나를 빼려면 레버 세트부터 들어내야 합니다.

5. H1 카시오형 해머(5.7점)
   - 보여주신 GIF와 가장 닮았고, 관성 93 g로 가장 피아노답습니다.
   - 하지만 세게 친 뒤 추가 되튀어 건반을 3~6 mm 차올려 유령 음이 날 수 있습니다.
   - 연타가 10.8 Hz로 목표(13.3 Hz)에 못 미치고, 펠트가 눌리면 덜걱 유격이 다시 생깁니다.

결론: W1을 기본으로 상세 설계에 들어갑니다. 여기에 다른 안의 좋은 점을 더합니다.
- S1: 천을 댄 피벗 홈, 손나사로 고정하는 업스톱 레일.
- v3: 앞 훅을 '닿지 않는 걸림쇠'로 되살림.
- 그랜드 피아노: 강철 캡스턴 나사(건반별 무게 조정).
- 검은 건반용 계단 스톱.
- 필요할 때만 끼우는 보조 스프링 자리.

단계 0 시편에서 y90의 무게가 거슬리면, 기판을 앞으로 옮겨 앞/뒤 비를 약 2.1로 낮추는 W1-B를 검토합니다.
